starting-off-dimintheis.speaker: Dimintheis
starting-off-dimintheis.text: Hello. My name is Dimintheis, of the noble family Fitzharmon.

options.text: Why would a nobleman live in a dump like this?

steps.player: Why would a nobleman live in a dump like this?

steps.speaker: Dimintheis
steps.text: The King has taken my estate from me until such time as I can show my family crest to him.

options.text: Why would he do that?

steps.player: Why would he do that?

steps.speaker: Dimintheis
steps.text: Well, there is a long standing rule of chivalry amongst the Varrockian aristocracy, where each noble family is in possession of a unique crest, which signifies the honour and lineage of the family. More than this

steps.speaker: Dimintheis
steps.text: however, it also represents the lawful rights of each family to prove their ownership of their wealth and lands. If the family crest is lost, then the family's estate is handed over to the current monarch until the crest is

steps.speaker: Dimintheis
steps.text: restored.

steps.speaker: Dimintheis
steps.text: This dates back to the times when there was much in-fighting amongst the noble families and their clans, and was introduced as a way of reducing the bloodshed that was devestating the ranks of the ruling classes at that

steps.speaker: Dimintheis
steps.text: time. When you captured a rival family's clan, you also captured their lands and wealth.
Continues from "So where is this crest?"

options.text: So where is this crest?

steps.player: So where is this crest?

steps.speaker: Dimintheis
steps.text: Well, my three sons took it with them many years ago when they rode out to fight in the war against the undead necromancer and his army in the battle to save Varrock.

steps.speaker: Dimintheis
steps.text: For many years I had assumed them all dead, as I had heard no word from them, but recently I heard word that my son Caleb is alive and well, and trying to earn his fortune as a great chef in the lands beyond White

steps.speaker: Dimintheis
steps.text: Wolf Mountain, although I know not where.

options.text: Yes.

steps.player: Ok, I will help you.

steps.speaker: Dimintheis
steps.text: I thank you greatly adventurer! Also... if you find Caleb... please... let him know his father still loves him...

options.text: No.

steps.player: I'm not interested in that adventure right now.

steps.speaker: Dimintheis
steps.text: I realise it was a lot to ask of a stranger.

options.text: You're rich then? Can I have some money?

steps.speaker: Dimintheis
steps.text: Gah! Lousy beggar! Your sort is what's ruining this great land! Why don't you just go and get a job if you need money so badly?

starting-off-dimintheis-talking-to-dimin.speaker: Dimintheis

options.text: Are you Caleb Fitzharmon?

steps.player: Are you Caleb Fitzharmon?

steps.text: Why... yes I am, but I don't believe I know you... how did you know my name?

steps.player: I have been sent by your father. He wishes the Fitzharmon Crest be restored.

steps.speaker: Caleb
steps.text: Ah... well... hmmm... yes... I do have a piece of it anyway...

options.text: Uh... what happened to the rest of it?

steps.player: Uh... what happened to the rest of it?

steps.speaker: Caleb
steps.text: Well... my brothers and I had a slight disagreement about it... we all wanted to be heir to my fathers' lands, and we each ended up with a piece of the crest.

steps.speaker: Caleb
steps.text: None of us wanted to give up our rights to our brothers, so we didn't want to give up our pieces of the crest, but none of us wanted to face our father by

steps.speaker: Caleb
steps.text: returning to him with an incomplete crest... We each went our seperate ways many years past, none of us seeing our father or willing to give up our fragments.

options.text: So can I have your bit?

steps.player: So can I have your bit?

steps.speaker: Caleb
steps.text: Well, I am the oldest son, so by the rules of chivalry, I am most entitled to be rightful bearer of the crest.

steps.player: It's not really much use without the other fragments is it though?

steps.speaker: Caleb
steps.text: Well that is true... perhaps it is time to put my pride aside... I'll tell you what: I'm struggling to complete this fish salad of mine,

steps.speaker: Caleb
steps.text: so if you will assist me in my search for the ingredients, then I will let you take my piece as reward for your assistance.

steps.player: So what ingredients are you missing?

steps.speaker: Caleb
steps.text: I require the following cooked fish: Swordfish, Bass, Tuna, Salmon and Shrimp.

options.text: Ok, I will get those.

steps.player: Ok, I will get those.

steps.text: You will? It would help me a lot!

options.text: Why don't you just give me the crest?

steps.speaker: Man
steps.text: stone available, and a necklace to match this ring.

steps.speaker: Man
steps.text: The problem however for me, is that not just any old gold will be suitable. I seek only the purest, the most high quality of gold - what I seek, if you will, is perfect gold.

steps.speaker: Man
steps.text: None of the gold around here is even remotely suitable in terms of quality. I have searched far and wide for the perfect gold I desire, but have had no success so in finding it.

steps.speaker: Man

options.text: I'll see what your brothers have to offer first.

steps.player: I'll see what your brothers have to offer first.

steps.speaker: Caleb
steps.text: As you wish. Let me know if you change your mind.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-avan-afte.speaker: Avan
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-avan-afte.text: I have received word from my father of your assistance to our family in this matter. You have my thanks for restoring our honour.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-avan-afte.player: Your father mentioned that you could improve these gauntlets in some way for me...

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-avan-afte.speaker: Avan
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-avan-afte.text: Indeed I can. In my long time searching for the 'perfect' gold I learned a lot about gold items. I can improve these gauntlets so that they provide more than normal

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-avan-afte.speaker: Avan
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-avan-afte.text: experience when smithing gold. I can easily modify these for you.

options.text: That sounds good, improve them for me.

steps.player: That sounds good, improve them for me!

steps.text: Avan takes your gauntlets, takes out a small hammer, and pounds them into a slightly new shape, then hands them back to you.

options.text: I think I'll check my other options with your brothers.

steps.player: I think I'll check my other options with your brothers before committing myself.

steps.speaker: Avan
steps.text: If you feel you really must consort with the likes of them. I await your decision.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-johnathon.speaker: Johnathon
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-johnathon.text: Hello again. My family now considers you a hero.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-johnathon.player: Your father tells me you can improve these gauntlets for me...

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-johnathon.speaker: Johnathon
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-johnathon.text: And right he is at that. Although my skill with Death Rune magiks was not great enough to defeat Chronozon, I am adequately skilled at Chaos Rune magiks.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-johnathon.speaker: Johnathon
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-johnathon.text: If you give me your gauntlets I will bestow upon them some of my power, and make any bolt spells you wish to cast more effective.

options.text: That sounds good to me.

steps.player: That sounds good to me!

steps.text: Johnathon takes your gauntlets from you, and begins a low chant over them. You see them begin to glow and sparkle, before he returns them to you.

options.text: I shall see what options your brothers can offer me first.

steps.player: I think I'll check my other options with your brothers before committing myself.

steps.speaker: Johnathon
steps.text: I doubt they will offer anything as useful as my magical boost, but as you wish.
